version_note: For claims backed by a fetchable web resource (a published page, a PR, a commit, a listing). When the platform has an API (GitHub, X), prefer E4 API query over fetching HTML. Judgment only runs on the fetched/extracted text content, never on raw pixels.
deterministic_precheck: URL resolves (HTTP 2xx) and is on an allowed domain (L1)
content fetched and reduced to text (L1 fetch, not model)
nonce present in fetched text when a nonce was issued
artifact_hash of fetched content not in dedup store
if platform API available: cross-check the resource via API (E4) instead of trusting HTML

criteria_met.instructions: Does the fetched content satisfy ALL of the acceptance criteria stated in state? Judge only whether the requirements are met.

content_authored.instructions: Does the content appear genuinely authored/published as claimed, rather than a placeholder, a draft, an unrelated page, or a page constructed only to pass this check?

supports_claim.instructions: Does the fetched content actually SUPPORT the specific claim being made, rather than merely being topically related to it?

evidence_quality.instructions: Overall credibility of this URL as proof of the claim.
criteria: does not support the claim / wrong page

posterior_rule.note: conjunctive. A page that is authored but does not support the claim must not pass.
